decision_conditions:
Condition : 1 - The development hereby permitted shall begin not later than three years from the date of this decision.
Reason: In order to comply with Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.
Condition : 2 - The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans and specifications: [Planning and Heritage Statement (dtd January 2025, by JMS Planning)Viability Statement (dtd January 2025, by JMS Planning), Preliminary Ecological Appraisal and Biodiversity Net Gain Assessment (dtd December 2024, by Ecology Partnership), Statutory Biodiversity Metric, Archaeological Desk-based Assessment (ref 10257/R01, Rev 2, dtd 18/12/2024,  by PCA Heritage), Air Quality assessment (AQ2252), Drainage Assessment Form, Fire Safety statement (Rev 4.0, dtd December 2024),  Sustainable Design and Construction Statement (Rev D, dtd December 2024, by JS Lewis ltd), Daylight and Sunlight Assessment (ref 2131/JN, dtd 15/01/2025, by Daylight and Sunlight ltd) � Received 22/01/2025; 23005-GAA-A2-XX-DR-T-0121(C01), 23005-GAA-A2-XX-DR-T-0122 (C03), 23005-GAA-A2-XX-DR-T-0123 (C05), 23005-GAA-A2-XX-DR-T-0124 (C03), 23005-GAA-A2-00-DR-T-2010 (C04), 23005-GAA-A2-00-DR T-2011(C04), 23005-GAA-A2-00-DR T-2012(C03), 23005-GAA-A2-00-DR T-2110(C05), 23005-GAA-A2-00-DR T-2111(C03), 23005-GAA-A2-00-DR T-2112(C04), 23005-GAA-A2-00-DR T-2210(C02), Design and Access Statement (ref 23005-GAA-A2-XX-DA-T-0001 (C02), dtd 22/04/2025, by GAA), Designers Response to Stage 1/ 2 Road Safety Audit, Parking Stress report ( V 3.0), Transport Statement (V 5.0), Noise Impact Assessment (VA4676.250422.NIA2.2, dtd 22/04/2025), Kitchen Odour Assessment (J0962/1/F1, dtd 23/04/2025)- Received 23/04/2025; Surface Water Drainage Strategy (Rev E) � Received 02/06/2025].
Reason: In order to ensure the development is carried out in accordance with the planning permission.
Condition : 3 - The development shall not be carried out other than in accordance with the submitted material details hereby approved.  
Reason.  In order to protect the appearance of the area thereafter.
Condition : 4 - No additional windows or openings shall be formed in the side elevations of the development hereby permitted.
Reason: In order to protect neighbours' privacy.
Condition : 5 - The dwellinghouses hereby permitted shall remain in use as a dwellinghouse(s) within the meaning of Class C3 of Schedule 1 to the Use Classes Order and for no other purpose, except to the extent that the other purpose is ancillary to the use as a dwellinghouse.
Reason: The Council is satisfied that the use hereby permitted would not result in detriment to adjoining properties but would wish to control future changes of use within the same Use Class to protect nearby land uses and the character of the area.
Condition : 6 - Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development Order) 1995 (or any order revoking or re-enacting that order), no enlargement of the new dwellings hereby permitted or any additional structures/ buildings/ enclosures within the curtilage of any dwelling shall be carried out, other than as shown in the approved drawings and no areas of hardstanding forward of the front elevations of the dwellings (other than as shown on the approved plans) shall be developed.
Reason:  To protect neighbours' living conditions and the character and appearance of the area and to prevent over-intensive use of the site.
Condition : 7 - a) The hereby approved development must be carried out in accordance with the energy strategy set out in the Sustainable Design and Construction Statement.
b) Prior to first occupation of any building within the development hereby approved evidence (e.g. photographs, installation contracts and to include As-Built certificates under the Standard Assessment Procedure/National Calculation Method) shall be submitted to the local planning authority and approved in writing to show that the development has been constructed in accordance with the approved Energy Strategy, and any subsequent approved revisions.
c) Prior to first occupation of the hereby approved development, where a contribution is found necessary to achieve compliance with zero-carbon requirements of the Development Plan, the developer shall have entered into a binding agreement with the Local Planning Authority to pay any carbon offset contribution at the published rate in-force at the time of submitting details pursuant to Part B of this condition. 
Reason: To ensure that the development makes the fullest contribution to minimising carbon dioxide emissions.
Condition : 8 - a)	No development above ground level shall take place until details have been submitted to and approved by the local planning authority which demonstrate that:
-	At least three of the key elements of the building envelope (external walls, windows roof, upper floor slabs, internal walls, floor finishes/coverings) are to achieve a rating of A+ to D in the Building Research Establishment (BRE) The Green Guide of specification.
-	At least 50% of timber and timber products are to be sourced from accredited Forest Stewardship Council (FSC) or Programme for the Endorsement of Forestry Certification (PEFC) scheme.
-	No construction or insulation materials are to be used which would release toxins into the internal and external environment, including those that deplete stratospheric ozone.
b)	The development shall not be occupied until evidence (e.g. photographs and copies of installation contracts) has been submitted to the local planning authority to demonstrate that the development has been carried out in accordance with the approved details under Part A of this condition. The development shall be maintained in accordance with the approved details at all times thereafter.
Reason: In the interests of sustainable development. 
Condition : 9 - Prior to first occupation of the building(s) hereby approved, the development shall have been constructed to achieve an internal water use of 105 litres/person/day or less.
Reason: In order to protect and conserve water supplies and resources.
Condition : 10 - The hereby approved development must be carried out in accordance with the approved Air Quality Assessment.
Reason: In the interests of air quality and to protect neighbours' living conditions and the wider local environment.
Condition : 11 - (a) No development (except any demolition, site clearance, ground investigation and remediation work) shall take place until details have been submitted to and approved by the local planning authority of a scheme providing enhanced sound insulation of the building envelope for properties numbered 6, 5 and 4 on the submitted plans, against the transmission of externally generated noise, taking account of any ventilation requirements necessary. The submitted details shall ensure enhancement of the building envelope to achieve internal sound levels resulting from public house activity of 10 dB below those specified in Table 4 of the British Standard 8233:2014 (Leq NR15 for music) are achieved at all times.
(b) Before the development hereby permitted is first occupied or brought into use, post-completion noise tests shall be carried out by accredited/approved organisations with competence in environmental noise assessments for residential accommodation and test reports shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. Noise tests shall be carried out taking account of worst-case environmental conditions and continuous logged data shall be submitted. 
Reason: In order to secure acceptable living conditions for residents of the new dwellings from noise generating activities of the neighbouring licensed premises.
Condition : 12 - Prior to commencement of the development, details shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Council, of an enhanced sound insulation value DnT,w of at least 5dB above the Building Regulations value, for the party wall structures separating properties 6, 5, 4 and 3 as numbered on the submitted plans. Approved details shall be implemented prior to occupation of the development and thereafter be permanently retained.
Reason: To ensure that the amenity of occupiers of the development site is not adversely affected by household/neighbour noise transmission of adjoining dwellings.
Condition : 13 - Prior to commencement of groundworks (excluding site investigations and demolition), the applicant must submit a final detailed drainage design including drawings and supporting calculations and updated Drainage Assessment Form to the Lead Local Flood Authority for review and approval, aligned with the Surface Water Drainage Strategy Rev E (May 2025) and associated drawings. A detailed management plan confirming routine maintenance tasks for all drainage components must also be submitted to demonstrate how the drainage system is to be maintained for the lifetime of the development. A maintenance owner should be provided.
Reason: To prevent the risk of flooding to and from the site in accordance with relevant policy requirements including but not limited to London Plan Policy SI 13, its associated Sustainable Design and Construction SPG, the Non-Statutory Technical Standards for Sustainable Drainage Systems and Hounslow Council's Local Plan Policy EQ3.
Condition : 14 - No building hereby permitted shall be occupied until evidence (photographs and installation contracts) is submitted to demonstrate that the sustainable drainage scheme for the site has been completed in accordance with the submitted details. The sustainable drainage scheme shall be managed and maintained thereafter in accordance with the agreed management and maintenance plan for all of the proposed drainage components.
Reason: To comply with the Non-Statutory Technical Standards for Sustainable Drainage Systems, the National Planning Policy Framework (Paragraph 103), the London Plan (Policies SI 12 and SI 13) along with associated guidance to these policies and Hounslow Council's Local Plan Policy EQ3.
Condition : 15 - No development shall take place until a Construction Logistics Plan (CLP), written in accordance with current TfL guidance, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The CLP shall include: 
(a)	a site plan (showing the elements set out below);
(b)	confirmation that a pre-start record of site conditions on the adjoining public highway will be undertaken with Hounslow Highways and a commitment to repair any damage caused;
(c)	provision for the parking of vehicles of site operatives and visitors;
(d)	provisions for loading, unloading and storage of plant and materials within the site;
(e)	details of access to the site, including means to control and manage access and egress of vehicles to and from the site for the duration of construction including phasing arrangements;
(f)	details of vehicle routeing from the site to the wider strategic road network;
(g)	the erection and maintenance of security hoarding including decorative displays and facilities for public viewing, where appropriate;
(h)	provision of wheel washing facilities at the site exit and a commitment to sweep adjacent roads when required and at the request of the Council;
(i)	a scheme for recycling/disposing of waste resulting from demolition and construction works; 
(j)	measures to ensure the safety of all users of the public highway especially cyclists and pedestrians in the vicinity of the site and especially at the access;
(k)	commitment to liaise with other contractors in the vicinity of the site to maximise the potential for consolidation and to minimise traffic impacts;
(l)	avoidance of peak hours for deliveries and details of a booking system to avoid vehicles waiting on the public highway;
(m)	all necessary traffic orders and other permissions required to allow safe access to the site to be secured and implemented prior to commencement of construction;(n)	details of the construction programme and a schedule of traffic movements;
(o)	the use of opera
Condition : 16 - Before the development hereby permitted is first occupied or brought into use, a Parking Management Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Plan shall include the following:
a)	details of parking allocations for residents of the approved development and how this will be operated and enforced
b)	details of measures proposed to restrict parking to designated bays only and prohibit parking on the access road
c)	a commitment to convert passive EV bays to active when demand requires.
d)	details of the operation of any gates or barriers
e)	measures to ensure that all prospective residents are informed of the Parking Management Plan and that all future residents will not be assigned a parking space or a right to park within the development other than blue badge holders.
The parking areas and access road(s) shall thereafter be managed in compliance with the approved Parking Management Plan, unless the prior written approval of the local planning authority is obtained to secure any variation.
Reason: In order to promote sustainable modes of transport, to protect neighbours' living conditions and to ensure minimal disruption of traffic in the locality.
Condition : 17 - Before the development hereby permitted is first occupied or brought into use, a Delivery & Servicing Plan (including details of vehicle access and egress arrangements and times that servicing shall take place) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall accord with current guidance such as that issued by TfL and include measures required to ensure sufficient arrangements (physical as well as managerial) for the servicing, including refuse collection, of all aspects of the development, the timing of hours for deliveries by motor vehicles and a timetable for implementation. The development shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the approved details and shall be maintained for the lifetime of the development, unless the prior written approval of the local planning authority is obtained to any variation.
Reason: In the interests of the safety of pedestrians and vehicles, to protect neighbours' living conditions and to support sustainable transport objectives.
Condition : 18 - Notwithstanding the submitted details and prior to occupation, full details (including manufacturer's specifications) of all cycle stands for the occupants of, and visitors to, the development shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The cycle parking shall conform to West London Cycle Parking Guidance or any such document that supersedes it.
The approved facilities shall be fully implemented and made available for use before any part of the development is first occupied and thereafter retained for use at all times without obstruction.
Reason: In order to support sustainable transport objectives.
Condition : 19 - No part of the development hereby approved shall be occupied or brought into use until that part of the road or vehicular access which provides access to it has been constructed in accordance with the approved plans. 
Reason: In order to protect the appearance of the and in the interests of highway safety.
Condition : 20 - Either side of the vehicle access hereby approved, visibility splay areas (the depth measured from the back of the footway and the widths outwards from the edges of the access, with a splay of at least 2.4 metres x 2.4 metres) shall be provided before the access and parking area is brought into use.  These areas shall be kept clear of any obstructions to visibility greater than 600 mm in height, including shrubs, planting, boundary walls, fences, gates, other means of enclosure or other structures or objects at all times.
Reason:  To ensure adequate visibility for drivers entering and leaving the site in the interests of pedestrian and vehicle safety.
Condition : 21 - Before the vehicle access hereby approved is first brought into use, the existing vehicular access on Staines Road as shown on dwg ref: 23005-GAA-A2-XX-DR-T-0123 (C05) shall be permanently closed and footway reinstated so that it cannot be used as a vehicle access across the pavement.
Reason: In order to enhance the pedestrian environment and to confine vehicular access to the permitted points to ensure that the development does not prejudice the free flow of traffic or highway safety along the adjacent highway.
Support notes: The applicant is advised that a supporting highways application should be submitted and approved prior to commencement of these works. 
Condition : 22 - The hardstanding hereby permitted shall be made of porous materials, or include provision to direct surface water run-off to a permeable or porous area or surface within the application site, in accordance with the (then) Department for Communities and Local Government publication "Guidance on the permeable surfacing of front gardens" dated September 2008 [before the building(s) hereby permitted is first occupied or brought into use]. The run-off shall not drain into any other foul or surface water drainage system. 
Reason: In order to reduce surface water run-off and the associated pressure on local drainage systems and so prevent flooding. 
Condition : 23 - Before the dwelling(s) hereby approved are first occupied, the developer shall provide to each dwelling a set of containers required at the time of development for household use for the storage and collection of recyclable materials for the purposes of the Council's kerbside recycling service, to the specification then in use by the local authority's recycling collection service and shall notify the Council's refuse and recycling services when the development is first occupied.  The waste and recyclable materials containers shall be stored in a proprietary refuse bin enclosure designed for the purpose to be supplied by the developer and located adjacent to each dwelling. Each dwelling with a private garden shall also be supplied with a garden waste composting bin of at least 220 litres capacity at the same time.
Reason: In order to protect the quality of the local environment and neighbours' living conditions and to endure appropriate means of refuse storage are provided.
Condition : 24 - Land quality � Preliminary Risk Assessment (Phase 1 desk study)
Prior to commencement of the development hereby approved:
No development shall take place until a preliminary non-intrusive risk assessment (Phase I desk study report) to identify possible areas and sources of land contamination which may exist on the site has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.  It will establish what intrusive investigation or site remediation measures may be necessary before the development commences. This report will be prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person.
Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.
Supporting notes: 
(i)	The Phase I desk study report will include the aims and objectives, data collection, site reconnaissance (walk over survey) and development of the initial Conceptual Site Model (CSM) with preliminary risk assessment whereby risk of all potential pollutant linkages are evaluated with a risk category. 
(ii)	The report must adhere to current UK guidance and best practice.
(iii)	The report shall also make recommendations for the further gathering of information and/or intrusive investigation, to ensure that it will be possible to render the site safe for its proposed use.
(iv)	The Council requests that the risk assessment reports or site plans are sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the local planning authority for approval.
Condition : 25 - Land quality - intrusive site investigation
Prior to commencement of the development hereby approved:
Following the completion of the Phase I desk study report, if intrusive investigations or gas monitoring is recommended, a Phase II site investigation must be undertaken.
No development other than necessary works to enable intrusive investigations shall take place until a Phase II site investigation report, prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.
This report shall identify the areas and sources of land contamination that exist on the site and identify the scope of site remediation measures necessary before the development commences.
The investigation shall be carried out by a competent person(s), based on the initial Conceptual Site Model (CSM) and on-site observations, to identify the extent and nature of contaminants. The initial CSM shall be updated accordingly following a tiered risk assessment based on the findings of the investigation, and where applicable, the report shall include proposals to deal with the identified contamination on site.
Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.
Supporting Notes:
(i)	The report shall include details of such sampling of soil, soil vapour, ground gas, leachate, surface water and/or groundwater at such locations and depths as are considered to characterise the site conditions based on the initial Conceptual Site Model (CSM) and on-site observations during investigation work. 
(ii)	The investigation and the report must adhere to current UK guidance and best practice.
(iii)	Further investigation shall be carried out at such locations and at such depths as the local planning authority may stipulate if this report  is found to be i
Condition : 26 - Land quality � Remediation Method Statement/ Remediation Strategy
Prior to commencement of the development hereby approved:
If a scheme for remediation is recommended in the Phase II site investigation for the site, no development shall take place until a remediation method statement prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person to specify the works necessary to render the site suitable for its proposed end use, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.
Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.
Supporting Notes:
(i)	The remediation method statement shall provide suitable details of how the risks of each pollutant linkages, as identified in the updated Conceptual Site Model, will be mitigated.
(ii)	The report shall account for any comments made by the local planning authority. 
(iii)	Remediation work shall be carried out in accordance with the approved remediation method statement for verification and validation before the development is first brought into use.
(iv)	The Council requests that remediation method statement or site plans be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the local planning authority for approval.
Condition : 27 - Land quality � additional/unexpected contamination found during development
During the development:
The Local Planning Authority shall be notified immediately if any land contamination not previously identified is encountered during development. A competent person shall assess the contamination, where necessary, including soil and groundwater sampling and testing before any further part of the development that may be affected by the additional contamination that has been discovered continues.
A revised remediation method statement, prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person, shall be submitted in writing to the local planning authority for approval within one month of the discovery of such contamination.
Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.
Supporting notes:
(i)	Further remediation work to remove or manage additional contamination shall be carried out in accordance with the approved revised remediation method statement for verification and validation before the development is first brought into use. 
(ii)	In some instances, the local planning authority may require work on site to be ceased whilst the nature of additional contamination is investigated fully.
(iii)	The Council requests that the revised remediation method statement or any site photos be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the local planning authority for approval.
Condition : 28 - Land quality - verification and validation of remedial work
Prior to the development is first brought into use:
The agreed scheme for remediation, including any amendments, shall be fully implemented. A verification report produced upon completion of the remediation by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person shall be submitted in writing to the local planning authority for approval, before the development is first brought into use or in accordance with a programme approved in writing by the local planning authority.
Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.
Supporting notes:
(i)	The verification (closure) report shall revisit the conceptual site model and provide evidence that each aspect of the remediation plan has been implemented correctly and successfully in accordance with current UK guidance and best practice. Where applicable, the report shall describe how any additional/unexpected contamination encountered during development has been managed in line with the revised remediation method statement. 
(ii)	This report shall demonstrate that the development is suitable for its proposed use in terms of land quality.
(iii)	The Council requests that the verification report or site photos be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the local planning authority for approval.
Condition : 29 - Land quality - long term monitoring and maintenance
If long term monitoring and maintenance is required following successful completion of approved remedial measures, reports which demonstrate the effectiveness of the monitoring and maintenance shall be prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person and submitted to the local planning authority according to an agreed timescale as shall first have been approved under other conditions set out in this planning approval decision notice.
This shall be conducted in accordance with current UK guidance and best practice.
Reason: In order to ensure that risks from land contamination to the future users of the land and neighbouring land are minimised, together with those to controlled waters, properties and ecological systems.
Condition : 30 - 
Notwithstanding any details included in the submitted plans, no development above ground level (except any demolition, site clearance, ground investigation and remediation work) shall take place until details of both hard and soft landscape works have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. These details shall include:  
a)	a statement setting out the design objectives and how these will be delivered;  
b)	pedestrian and vehicle access and circulation areas, materials, means of enclosure/boundary treatment(s) and retaining structures; 
c)	minor artefacts and structures where relevant (e.g. furniture, play equipment, refuse or other storage units, signs, lighting, renewable energy installations, CCTV, indicative services layout, etc.); 
d)	retained historic or other landscape features and proposals for restoration, where relevant; 
e)	planting plans, written specifications (including cultivation and other operations associated with plant and grass establishment); schedules of plants, noting species, plant sizes and proposed numbers and densities where appropriate; and
f)	an implementation programme (including phasing of work where relevant).
The landscaping works shall comply with the requirements specified in BS 3936 (1992) 'Specification of Nursery Stock Part 1 Trees and Shrubs', and in BS 4428 (1989) 'Recommendations for General Landscape Operations', and shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details before the development hereby permitted is first occupied or brought into use, or such other date(s) as may be specified in the agreed implementation programme.
Any trees or plants that, within 5 years of planting, die, are cut down, uprooted, destroyed or become (in the opinion of the Local Planning Authority) seriously damaged or defective, shall be replaced with another tree or plant of the same size and species within the first planting season following its death, removal, uprooting or destruction, unless
Condition : 31 - Prior to the first commencement of the hereby approved development, a Biodiversity Gain Plan shall  be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, the Plan shall include; (a) information about the steps taken or to be taken to minimise the adverse effect of the development on the biodiversity of the onsite habitat and any other habitat, (b) the pre-development biodiversity value of the onsite habitat, (c) the post-development biodiversity value of the onsite habitat, (d) any registered offsite biodiversity gain allocated to the development and the biodiversity value of that gain in relation to the development, (e) any biodiversity credits purchased for the development, and (f) such other matters as the Secretary of State may by regulations specify. The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved Plan prior to the first occupation of the development. Any habitats created or enhanced on-site and off-site in accordance with the Biodiversity Gain Plan must be maintained thereafter for a minimum of 30 years. 
Reason. In the interests of improving Biodiversity and in accordance with The Town and Country Planning Act 1990, Section 90A, Schedule 7A. 
Condition : 32 - 
Notwithstanding the submitted details, no above ground works, excluding demolition, remediation and groundworks, shall take place until a habitat management plan in accordance with the approved Biodiversity Gain Plan must be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. 
The habitat management plan shall include:
a)	Prescription for management actions.
b)	Preparation of the work schedule (including an annual work Plan for over 30-year period and who will carry out the jobs mentioned in the management plans).
c)	Details of the body or organisation responsible for implementation of the plan.
d)	Time frame for reviewing the plan.
e)	Details of the management plans and its communication to the occupiers of the development.
Reason: In the interests of improving Biodiversity and in accordance with The Town and Country Planning Act 1990, Section 90A, Schedule 7A.
Condition : 33 - No demolition or development shall take place until a stage 1 written scheme of investigation (WSI) has been submitted to and approved by the local planning authority in writing. For land that is included within the WSI, no demolition or development shall take place other than in accordance with the agreed WSI, and the programme and methodology of site evaluation and the nomination of a competent person(s) or organisation to undertake the agreed works.
If heritage assets of archaeological interest are identified by stage 1 then for those parts of the site which have archaeological interest a stage 2 WSI shall be submitted to and approved by the local planning authority in writing. For
land that is included within the stage 2 WSI, no demolition/development shall take place other than in accordance with the agreed stage 2 WSI which shall include:
A.The statement of significance and research objectives, the programme and methodology of site investigation and recording and the nomination of a competent person(s) or organisation to undertake the agreed works
B. Where appropriate, details of a programme for delivering related positive public benefits
C. The programme for post-investigation assessment and subsequent analysis, publication & dissemination and deposition of resulting material.
This part of the condition shall not be discharged until these elements have been fulfilled in accordance with the programme set out in the stage 2 WSI.
Informative: 
Written schemes of investigation will need to be prepared and implemented by a suitably professionally accredited archaeological practice in accordance with Historic England's Guidelines for Archaeological Projects in Greater
London. This condition is exempt from deemed discharge under schedule 6 of The Town and Country Planning (Development Management Procedure) (England) Order 2015.
